Achmetha
AK-meh-thah
proper noun
Aramaic Achmetha, the city of Ecbatana, capital of Media, where the decree of Cyrus concerning the temple was found in the royal archives.

Biblical Definition

Achmetha, the Ecbatana of the Medes, is the place where a lost decree was found and a great work saved. When the enemies of the returned exiles challenged their right to rebuild the temple, Darius ordered a search of the records, “and there was found at Achmetha, in the palace that is in the province of the Medes, a roll, and therein was a record thus written” (Ezr 6:2). The search had begun in Babylon — “search was made in the house of the rolls, where the treasures were laid up in Babylon” (Ezr 6:1) — but it was in the summer palace of Achmetha that the decree of Cyrus lay preserved: “In the first year of Cyrus the king the same Cyrus the king made a decree concerning the house of God at Jerusalem, Let the house be builded” (Ezr 6:3). On the strength of that recovered scroll, Darius confirmed the work and commanded its costs to be paid from the royal treasury. Achmetha is a quiet monument to the providence that governs archives and kings. A pagan decree, filed years before and forgotten by men, was kept by God in a Median palace against the very day His people needed it. “The king’s heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will” (Pro 21:1). The temple rose because God had hidden a scroll in Achmetha.

Webster 1828 Definition

Ecbatana, the Median capital where the lost decree of Cyrus was found (Ezr 6:2); a monument to the providence that guards archives and turns the hearts of kings.

ACHMETHA, the city of Ecbatana, capital of Media.

A royal residence with archives of the Persian empire.

There the decree of Cyrus for the temple was found (Ezr 6:2).

On its strength Darius confirmed the rebuilding (Ezr 6:3).

A monument to providence that preserves records against the day of need.

Ezr 6:2 — "And there was found at Achmetha, in the palace that is in the province of the Medes, a roll, and therein was a record thus written:"

Ezr 6:1 — "Then Darius the king made a decree, and search was made in the house of the rolls, where the treasures were laid up in Babylon."

Ezr 6:3 — "In the first year of Cyrus the king the same Cyrus the king made a decree concerning the house of God at Jerusalem, Let the house be builded,"

Pro 21:1 — "The king's heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will."

Modern Corruption

Ecbatana, where the lost decree of Cyrus was found; the entry recovers the providence that guards archives and turns the hearts of kings for His church.

expand to see more

Achmetha raises no modern controversy, yet the finding of the scroll rebukes the notion that the work of God hangs upon human vigilance alone. A decree filed and forgotten in a Median palace was the hinge on which the whole rebuilding turned. Men had lost it; God had kept it.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the meticulous providence of God over the smallest instruments of His purpose — a filed roll, a king’s memory, a clerk’s search. He turns the heart of Darius as He turned the heart of Cyrus, for the king’s heart is in His hand as the rivers of water (Pro 21:1). The church builds under the eye of a God who prepared her provisions before she knew her need, hiding a scroll in Achmetha against the day of Darius. What men mislay, God preserves; what enemies would forbid, He commands to be paid from their own treasury.

"On the decree recovered at Achmetha, Darius upheld the temple work."

"Achmetha preaches the providence that preserves a scroll against the day of need."
